claims.text: Increasing grain-boundary density will increase the coercive field in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Inducing nanoprecipitates will increase the coercive field in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
The initial as-cast alloy is homogeneous and has relatively coarse grains.
Controlled cold rolling followed by tailored annealing can produce a refined grain structure.
Controlled cold rolling followed by tailored annealing can produce dispersed nanoprecipitates.
Excessive grain growth or precipitate coarsening would undermine the intended microstructural refinement.
The treatment is expected to increase grain-boundary density.
The treatment is expected to create well-dispersed nanoprecipitates.
Grain boundaries and nanoprecipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Greater domain-wall pinning makes domain-wall motion more difficult.
More difficult domain-wall motion increases the coercive field.
The processed alloy will have a higher coercive field than an as-cast or non-cold-rolled control.
Adverse phase transformations can diminish the proposed pinning effect.
Excessive grain growth can diminish the proposed pinning effect.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase depends on the processing parameters.

contradictions.description: The boundary makes the predicted coercivity increase conditional on successful microstructural refinement, but the falsification rule says that failure to produce the expected refinement itself falsifies the hypothesis. Failure to realize a stated prerequisite tests the intervention implementation rather than decisively refuting the conditional mechanism.
